scenarioStory.history: Wife reports increasing shortness of breath over the past two days, now with much more labored breathing and increasing drowsiness over the last hour. He has been using his home nebulizer more frequently without relief.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 72-year-old male with severe COPD in tripod position, using accessory muscles, with a prolonged expiratory phase and increasing drowsiness suggestive of developing CO2 retention/narcosis. → CPAP and in-line duoneb started: Crew initiates CPAP with in-line albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer via a T-connector, titrating supplemental oxygen to a permissive-hypoxia target appropriate for this patient's chronic COPD rather than chasing a normal saturation. → CPAP seal maintained, improved and transported: The patient's mental status and work of breathing continue to improve on CPAP with in-line bronchodilator therapy. Crew maintains a continuous CPAP seal throughout transport per protocol, avoiding any interruption.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Severe shortness of breath, worsening over 2 days

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 72-year-old male with severe COPD in tripod position, using accessory muscles, with a prolonged expiratory phase and increasing drowsiness suggestive of developing CO2 retention/narcosis.
relatedChecklist: Initiate CPAP for severe respiratory distress with developing CO2 retention
Administer albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer in-line with CPAP via T-connector
Titrate oxygen to a permissive-hypoxia target of SpO2 ≥ 90%, not a normal saturation
Monitor EtCO2 trend for downward direction rather than expecting full normalization

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP and in-line duoneb started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew initiates CPAP with in-line albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer via a T-connector, titrating supplemental oxygen to a permissive-hypoxia target appropriate for this patient's chronic COPD rather than chasing a normal saturation.
relatedChecklist: Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal throughout transport until hospital CPAP is ready to take over

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP seal maintained, improved and transported
scenarioEvents.description: The patient's mental status and work of breathing continue to improve on CPAP with in-line bronchodilator therapy. Crew maintains a continuous CPAP seal throughout transport per protocol, avoiding any interruption.

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP delayed, CO2 narcosis worsens
scenarioEvents.description: Crew continues only low-flow oxygen and standard nebulizer without escalating to CPAP. The patient's mental status continues to deteriorate as EtCO2 climbs, consistent with worsening CO2 narcosis and impending respiratory failure.
relatedChecklist: Recognize CO2 narcosis (worsening somnolence, rising EtCO2, falling RR); initiate CPAP with in-line duoneb immediately

checklist.title: Initiate CPAP for severe respiratory distress with developing CO2 retention
Administer albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer in-line with CPAP via T-connector
Titrate oxygen to a permissive-hypoxia target of SpO2 ≥ 90%, not a normal saturation
Monitor EtCO2 trend for downward direction rather than expecting full normalization
Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal throughout transport until hospital CPAP is ready to take over
Recognize CO2 narcosis (worsening somnolence, rising EtCO2, falling RR); initiate CPAP with in-line duoneb immediately
